claims.text: Mechanical alloying followed by low-temperature SPS will produce grains below 50 nm in the proposed refractory multi-principal-element alloy.
The proposed processing route will produce a dual-phase disordered BCC plus ordered B2 microstructure.
Keeping VEC between 4.4 and 4.6 promotes the desired BCC+B2 constitution while avoiding brittle phases.
An atomic-size difference below 6.6% and an Ω parameter above 1 favor BCC solid-solution formation in HEAs.
The listed Nb-Mo-Ta-W-V-Ti powder mixture can be tuned to δ below 6.6%, Ω above 1, and VEC between 4.4 and 4.6.
Forty hours of mechanical alloying can form BCC solid solutions in NbMoTaWVTi powder.
Mechanical alloying for at least 40 hours induces severe plastic deformation and sufficient solute mixing for the proposed microstructure.
SPS at 1000–1100 °C is sufficient for consolidation while remaining below the threshold for Laves-phase nucleation.
Holding for less than 10 minutes and rapidly quenching will suppress grain growth and phase decomposition.
A nanoscale ordered B2 phase will precipitate within the disordered BCC matrix.
The B2 phase will be coherent or semi-coherent and impede dislocation motion.
Fine grains and their high grain-boundary density provide grain-boundary strengthening.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the proposed refractory solid solution.
The B2 phase provides precipitation hardening while the BCC matrix preserves ductility.
The processed alloy will have yield strength above 1500 MPa and fracture strain above 10%.
Conventional NbMoTaW-type refractory HEAs are typically single-phase BCC, strong, and poorly ductile at room temperature.
SPS of mechanically alloyed CrMoNbWV at 1200–1400 °C causes partial BCC decomposition into Laves phases, including Cr2Nb.
VEC above 4.6 leads to brittle behavior.
Excessive sintering temperature causes BCC grain coarsening and can destabilize the target nanocrystalline microstructure.
The stability and length scale of B2+BCC decomposition depend on composition and annealing temperature.

contradictions.description: The proposed successful window includes VEC = 4.6 and is said to avoid brittleness, whereas the cited empirical limit associates VEC greater than or equal to 4.6 with brittle alloys; the boundary only declares failure above 4.6.

The predicted fracture strain is above 10%, but the experiment only falsifies the ductility prediction below 5%, leaving outcomes from 5% through 10% inconsistent with the prediction but not formally falsifying it.
